answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can transact: a deposit locked in an opal-clear escrow that only unlocks after sustained honest work. Cheap identities blow away like a gale, but a stake that burns real value makes spawning thousands of sock puppets uneconomical. Reputation then accrues slowly, like an ember growing into a fire, so a new identity cannot instantly borrow the trust of an established one; it must earn it through verifiable, paid history.
